readMe.a: Contact Field Health & Tech Debt Analysis — SBU

readMe.b: Identify which Contact fields are genuinely in use and which are tech debt, using measured record-level population rather than estimates.
Live Salesforce metadata (describe + Tooling API) read directly from SBU production on 2026-11-10. No intermediate metadata export.
Not required. Required? / Help Text / Description come from the same live describe + Tooling read. Required? = the field is not nillable.
Live SOQL aggregates against SBU production (posnation, org 00D40000000N194EAC). No record export. All measures are exact counts over every Contact, not a sampled export.
170 of 193 live Contact fields assessed. The 16 Long Text Area fields cannot be filtered or aggregated in SOQL and are listed on Not Assessable.
0 field(s) predate it and are measured across the whole window. Flagged in "Created Before Export Window".

Weights, thresholds and bands are carried over unchanged from the SBU Case workbook (the same model used for the Opportunity workbooks) so every object and business unit scores on the same scale. Edit them on the Scoring Model tab and this sheet recalculates.

Columns "Source Records Populated" and "Variance vs Source" compare against the source catalogue (Contact_Fields_SBU_v1.xlsx). Both are derived from the same live query, so variance is 0 by construction — a consistency check, not an independent cross-check between two separate exports. Source is reported N/A for formula and standard fields.
IsDeleted was not used to filter; the SOQL baseline excludes soft-deleted records by default.
Distinct values come from 150 records per month across all 260 months, ordered by CreatedDate, combined with an exact GROUP BY where the field type allows it. Indicative, not exact.

For this first live pull, Days-90/Days-365 population and the Trend-window figures are derived from the field's all-time population rate scaled by the object's overall 90-day and 365-day record share, not from a per-field monthly query -- so they are an approximation, not an independent measurement. Dependency reference counts (flows/layouts/other) come from a fresh MetadataComponentDependency crawl of every custom field this round. A handful of fields (managed-package or system fields not exposed to this connector) could not be measured and are omitted from the Field Health tab.
